description: Əsas məqsədimiz, yalnız mürəkkəb elmi məlumatları emal etmək deyil, eyni zamanda onları başa düşülən və istifadə edilə bilən strateji məlumatlara çevirməkdir. Biz inanırıq ki, planetimizin üzləşdiyi ekoloji dəyişiklikləri daha yaxşı anlamaq və düzgün proqnozlaşdırmaq üçün kosmik məlumatlardan daha effektiv istifadə edilməlidir. Bizim amalımız, süni intellekt və qabaqcıl vizuallaşdırma metodları ilə NASA-nın peyk məlumatlarını (Signal) təhlil edərək (Code), Yer kürəsinin gələcək inkişaf trayektoriyasını (Trajectory) proqnozlaşdırmaq və bu əsasda daha doğru qərarlar qəbul edilməsinə töhfə verməkdir. Bizim şüarımız da elə bu amalı əks etdirir: "Same Planet. Better Decisions. Bigger Impact."
summary:
Earth Fingerprint is an independent geospatial analytics platform, not an official NASA product. It examines several environmental variables together to find unusual ecological patterns in a region.

Problem: Ecological change is often tracked through one indicator. Yet temperature and precipitation can look normal while vegetation changes and evaporation behaves differently. The signal may sit in the combination of variables, which single-indicator analysis can miss. (Illustrative example, not a measured result.)

Core idea: Each region has an ecological fingerprint formed by how its variables behave together. The platform compares a region against a historical reference year, moving from single-variable analysis to multi-variable pattern discovery.

What it does: A working web product (https://earth-fingerprint.lovable.app/explore) lets users select a region on a map, choose an analysis period and a reference year, and run a quick analysis based on NASA POWER temperature and precipitation. An advanced mode integrating further NASA datasets is under processing and validation. NASA GIBS imagery is used for visuals only.

Built with: React, Tailwind CSS, MapLibre, Python, FastAPI, Pandas, NumPy, Plotly, Recharts.

Applications: drought and vegetation research, environmental monitoring, regional comparisons, decision support.

Future: broader coverage and more advanced multi-variable models (planned, not completed functionality).

Project Details: Earth Fingerprint

1. Project goal

Earth Fingerprint analyzes environmental indicators together rather than one at a time, in order to reveal unusual ecological patterns in different regions. It is an independent project, not an official NASA product. The main goal is to move from single-variable analysis to multi-variable ecological pattern discovery.

2. The problem

Ecological change is often tracked through a single indicator. The limitation of this approach is that each indicator can look normal while their joint behavior is unusual. For example, in one region temperature and precipitation may be normal while vegetation cover is changing and evaporation shows different dynamics. In such a case the signal appears only in the combination of variables. (This example is illustrative, not a measured result.)

3. Our approach

We treat each region as having its own “ecological fingerprint”, formed by how its environmental variables behave together. The platform helps surface unusual regional dynamics by comparing this behavior with a historical reference year. The approach has three core elements:

  • Multi-variable view: six environmental variables are considered together.
  • Historical context: the selected period is compared against a reference year chosen by the user.
  • Regional focus: each region is evaluated by its own profile.

4. How we used NASA data

The project uses two data sources:

  • NASA POWER: the main source for the quick analysis.
  • ORNL: used in the advanced POWER + ORNL analysis.

The analysis covers six variables: temperature, precipitation, evapotranspiration, soil moisture, NDVI and radiation. [Specify which source provides each variable.]

5. Workflow

  1. Data collection: NASA POWER and ORNL sources.
  2. Environmental variables: selection of the six indicators.
  3. Data processing: standardization and historical comparison.
  4. Analytics: [list the methods the team has actually implemented].
  5. Results: ecological patterns, comparisons and potential anomalies.

6. Existing platform features

Working product: https://earth-fingerprint.lovable.app/explore

  • Region selection and geographic exploration on a map
  • Selection of the analysis period
  • Selection of a historical reference year
  • Choice among six environmental variables
  • Quick NASA POWER analysis
  • Advanced POWER + ORNL analysis

7. Technology stack

  • Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, Vite 8
  • Backend: TypeScript, TanStack Start, Nitro, Supabase, Lovable Cloud
  • Data Processing: NASA POWER API, PostgreSQL, Statistical Analysis, ml-matrix
  • Machine Learning & AI: Lovable AI Gateway, AI-Powered Analysis
  • Visualization: Recharts, MapLibre GL JS, WebGL
  • Data Sources: NASA POWER, NASA GIBS, NASA AppEEARS (in development)
  • eployment: GitHub, Lovable, Vercel

8. Potential impact and applications

  • Drought and vegetation change research
  • Environmental monitoring
  • Regional ecological comparisons
  • Historical environmental pattern analysis
  • Scientific research and decision support

The platform does not deliver final conclusions. It gives researchers a tool to investigate environmental change through multiple indicators and historical context.

9. Limitations

  • Patterns the platform finds are treated as “potential anomalies”. Their ecological cause requires further scientific investigation.
  • The project does not report accuracy metrics or validation results.
  • Analysis quality depends on the spatial and temporal resolution of the source data. [Specify the resolution of your sources.]

10. Future development

  • Broader regional coverage
  • Expanded environmental anomaly analysis
  • More advanced multi-variable models

These are planned directions, not completed functionality.
